title.zh: 卷一百〇三 列傳第三十三: 文學上
title.raw: 卷一百〇三 列傳第三十三: 文學上 Volume 103 Biographies 33: Literature 1

sentences.zh: 文學上 ○蕭韓家奴李澣

translations.literal: Literature, Part One ○ Xiao Hanjianu, Li Han
translations.idiomatic: Literature 1 ○ Xiao Hanjianu · Li Han

sentences.zh: 遼起松漠，太祖以兵經略方內，禮文之事固所未遑。

translations.literal: Liao arose in Songmo; the Taizu Emperor used arms to bring the realm under control, and ritual and literary matters were certainly not yet attended to.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao state rose from the Songmo region. Emperor Taizu conquered the empire by force of arms, and court ritual and letters were naturally left for later.

sentences.zh: 及太宗入汴，取晉圖書、禮器而北，然後制度漸以修舉。

translations.literal: When the Taizong Emperor entered Bian, he took the Jin dynasty's books and ritual vessels northward; only then were institutions gradually put in order.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizong entered Bianjing and carried the Jin libraries and ritual vessels north, institutions were gradually restored.

sentences.zh: 至景、聖間，則科目聿興，士有由下僚擢升侍從，骎驍崇儒之美。

translations.literal: By the reigns of Jingzong and Shengzong, examination subjects flourished anew; scholars were raised from junior posts to attendants-in-waiting, and the beauty of honoring Confucian learning advanced swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Jingzong and Shengzong the civil-service examinations revived, and men rose from low office into the imperial entourage—a swift flowering of Confucian cultivation at court.

sentences.zh: 但其風氣剛勁，三面鄰敵，歲時以蒐浯為務，而典章文物，視古猶闕。

translations.literal: Yet its customs were stern and forceful; on three sides it bordered enemies, and year by year hunting and military drill were the chief tasks, while canonical statutes and cultural relics still fell short of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the realm's spirit remained martial and hard-edged. Enemies pressed on three fronts, and the seasons were given over to hunts and maneuvers; canonical law and cultural patrimony still lagged far behind the ancient model.

sentences.zh: 然二百年之業，非數君子為之綜理，則後世惡所考述哉？

translations.literal: Yet for a two-hundred-year enterprise, had not several gentlemen synthesized and ordered it, where would later ages find material for inquiry and narration?
translations.idiomatic: Still, two centuries of statecraft would have left later ages nothing to study had not a handful of scholars gathered and ordered the record.

sentences.zh: 作《文學傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Literature" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Literature."

sentences.zh: 蕭韓家奴，字休堅，涅剌部人，中書令安摶之孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Hanjianu, style name Xiujian, was a man of the Niela tribe, grandson of Chief Councillor An Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hanjianu, styled Xiujian, came from the Niela tribe and was a grandson of Chief Councillor An Tuo.

sentences.zh: 少好學，弱冠入南山讀書，博覽經史，通遼、漢文字。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; at twenty he entered the Southern Mountains to study, broadly reading the classics and histories and mastering both Khitan and Chinese script.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning from boyhood. At twenty he went into the Southern Mountains to read, mastered the classics and histories, and was fluent in both Khitan and Chinese writing.

sentences.zh: 統和十四年始仕。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tonghe he first entered office.
translations.idiomatic: He first took office in the fourteenth year of the Tonghe era.

sentences.zh: 家有一牛，不任驅策，其奴得善價鬻之。

translations.literal: His household had an ox that could not be driven; a servant obtained a good price and sold it.
translations.idiomatic: The family owned an ox that could not be driven. A servant found a good buyer and sold it.

sentences.zh: 韓家奴曰：「利己誤人，非吾所欲。」

translations.literal: Hanjianu said, "To profit oneself and harm another is not what I desire."
translations.idiomatic: Hanjianu said, "Profiting myself while wronging someone else is not what I want."

sentences.zh: 乃歸直取牛。

translations.literal: He then returned the payment and took back the ox.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the money and reclaimed the ox.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，為右通進，典南京栗園。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he became Right Vice Commissioner for Forwarding Memorials and supervised the chestnut orchards of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight of Tonghe he was made Right Vice Commissioner for Forwarding Memorials and put in charge of the Southern Capital's chestnut orchards.

sentences.zh: 重熙初，同知三司使事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongxi he served as Associate Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongxi era he became Associate Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷天成軍節度使，徙彰湣宮使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Tiancheng Army, then moved to Commissioner of Zhangmin Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year four of Chongxi he was promoted to Military Commissioner of Tiancheng Army, then transferred to Commissioner of Zhangmin Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝與語，才之，命為詩友。

translations.literal: The emperor conversed with him, recognized his talent, and appointed him a poetry companion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke with him, recognized his talent, and named him a poetry companion.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容問曰：「卿居外有異聞乎？」

translations.literal: Once, in an easy mood, he asked, "In your service outside the capital, have you heard anything unusual?"
translations.idiomatic: On one relaxed occasion the emperor asked, "In your posts away from court, have you heard anything noteworthy?"

sentences.zh: 韓家奴對曰：「臣惟知炒栗：小者熟，則大者必生；

translations.literal: Hanjianu replied, "Your servant knows only roasting chestnuts: when the small ones are done, the large ones must still be raw;
translations.idiomatic: Hanjianu answered, "Your servant knows only how to roast chestnuts: if the small ones are done, the large ones must still be raw;

sentences.zh: 大者熟，則小者必焦。

translations.literal: when the large ones are done, the small ones must be scorched.
translations.idiomatic: if the large ones are done, the small ones will be burnt.

sentences.zh: 使大小均熟，始為盡美。

translations.literal: Only when large and small are equally done is the perfection complete.
translations.idiomatic: Only when large and small are roasted alike is the result truly perfect.

sentences.zh: 不知其他。」

translations.literal: I know nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: I know nothing beyond that."

sentences.zh: 蓋嘗掌栗園，故托栗以諷諫。

translations.literal: For he had once managed the chestnut orchards and therefore used chestnuts as a vehicle for indirect remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He had once managed the chestnut orchards, and so he used chestnuts as a veiled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 詔作《四時逸樂賦》，帝稱善。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compose the "Rhapsody on Leisure and Pleasure through the Four Seasons," and the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to write the "Rhapsody on Leisure through the Four Seasons" and praised the result.

sentences.zh: 時詔天下言治道之要，制問：「徭役不加於舊，征伐亦不常有，年谷既登，帑廩既實，而民重困，豈為吏者慢、為民者惰歟？

translations.literal: At that time an edict summoned the realm to speak on the essentials of governance, with an imperial question: "Corvée is not increased beyond the old level, campaigns are not frequent, the year's grain is already harvested, and the treasury granaries are already full—yet the people are heavily distressed. Is it that officials are negligent and the people indolent?
translations.idiomatic: An edict then called on the empire to address the essentials of good government. The throne asked: "Corvée has not risen above former levels, campaigns are not constant, harvests are in, and the treasuries are full—yet the people remain deeply afflicted. Are officials negligent and the common folk lazy?

sentences.zh: 今之徭役何者最重？

translations.literal: Among present corvée duties, which is heaviest?
translations.idiomatic: Which corvée burden weighs most heavily today?

sentences.zh: 何者尤苦？

translations.literal: Which is most bitter?
translations.idiomatic: Which is most cruel?

sentences.zh: 何所蠲省則為便益？

translations.literal: What, if reduced or remitted, would bring convenience and benefit?
translations.idiomatic: What reductions would bring real relief?

sentences.zh: 補役之法何可以復？

translations.literal: How may the method of corvée replacement be restored?
translations.idiomatic: How can the corvée-replacement system be restored?

sentences.zh: 盜賊之害何可以止？」

translations.literal: How may the harm of banditry be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: How can banditry be stopped?"

sentences.zh: 韓家奴對曰：

translations.literal: Hanjianu replied:
translations.idiomatic: Hanjianu answered:

sentences.zh: 臣伏見比年以來，高麗未賓，阻卜猶強，戰守之備，誠不容已。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that in recent years Goryeo has not submitted, the Zubu remain strong, and preparations for war and defense truly cannot be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed that in recent years Goryeo has not submitted, the Zubu remain formidable, and preparations for war and defense cannot in truth be set aside.

sentences.zh: 乃者選富民防邊，自備糧糗。

translations.literal: Recently wealthy households have been selected to guard the frontier, supplying their own provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Lately wealthy households have been drafted to guard the frontier at their own expense.

sentences.zh: 道路修阻，動淹歲月；

translations.literal: Roads are long and difficult, and journeys often drag on for months;
translations.idiomatic: The roads are long and hard, and journeys often take months;

sentences.zh: 比至屯所，費已過半；

translations.literal: by the time they reach the garrison post, more than half their costs are already spent;
translations.idiomatic: by the time they reach the garrison, more than half their supplies are gone;

sentences.zh: 只牛單轂，鮮有還者。

translations.literal: with a single ox and one-wheeled cart, few ever return.
translations.idiomatic: with a lone ox and a single-wheeled cart, few ever come home again.

sentences.zh: 其無丁之家，倍直傭僦，人憚其勞，半途亡竄，故戍卒之食多不能給。

translations.literal: Households without able-bodied men pay double the fair price to hire substitutes; men fear the labor and flee midway, so the food of garrison soldiers often cannot be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Households without able-bodied men pay double the going rate to hire substitutes. Men dread the labor and desert halfway, so frontier garrisons often go without food.

sentences.zh: 求假於人，則十倍其息，至有鬻子割田不能償者。

translations.literal: When they borrow from others, interest is tenfold; some even sell children or mortgage fields and still cannot repay.
translations.idiomatic: When they borrow, interest runs tenfold; some sell their children or mortgage their fields and still cannot pay the debt.

sentences.zh: 或逋役不歸，在軍物故，則復補以少壯。

translations.literal: Some evade service and do not return; if a man dies in the army, the young and strong are drafted again to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Some flee service and never return. When a soldier dies on campaign, the young and strong are conscripted again to fill the gap.

sentences.zh: 其鴨淥江之東，戍役大率如此。

translations.literal: East of the Yalu River, frontier service is largely like this.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yalu River, frontier service is largely the same.

sentences.zh: 況渤海、女直、高麗合從連衡，不時征討。

translations.literal: Moreover, Bohai, Jurchen, and Goryeo form alliances and leagues, and campaigns are launched from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Bohai, the Jurchen, and Goryeo form shifting alliances, and expeditions are mounted without cease.

sentences.zh: 富者從軍，貧者偵候。

translations.literal: The wealthy go to war; the poor serve as scouts.
translations.idiomatic: The rich go to war; the poor serve as scouts.

sentences.zh: 加之水旱，菽粟不登，民以日困。

translations.literal: Added to this are flood and drought; grain does not ripen, and the people grow daily more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts follow, grain fails, and the people grow poorer by the day.

sentences.zh: 蓋勢使之然也。

translations.literal: It is the force of circumstances that makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstance alone drives this outcome.

sentences.zh: 方今最重之役，無過西戍。

translations.literal: Among present duties, none is heavier than garrison service in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Today no corvée weighs more heavily than service on the western frontier.

sentences.zh: 如無西戍，雖遇凶年，困弊不至於此。

translations.literal: Without western garrison duty, even in bad years distress would not reach this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Without the western garrisons, even in famine years distress would not run so deep.

sentences.zh: 若能徙西戍稍近，則往來不勞，民無深患。

translations.literal: If western garrisons could be moved somewhat nearer, travel back and forth would not be so burdensome and the people would not suffer so deeply.
translations.idiomatic: If the western garrisons were shifted somewhat nearer, travel would be less punishing and the people's affliction would ease.

sentences.zh: 議者謂徙之非便：一則損威名，二則召侵侮，三則棄耕牧之地。

translations.literal: Those who debate say relocation would be inexpedient: first, it would diminish prestige; second, it would invite aggression; third, it would abandon lands for farming and herding.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say relocation would be unwise: it would diminish prestige, invite attack, and abandon cultivated and pastured lands.

sentences.zh: 臣謂不然。

translations.literal: Your servant says this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant disagrees.

sentences.zh: 阻卜諸部，自來有之。

translations.literal: The various Zubu tribes have existed from of old.
translations.idiomatic: The Zubu tribes have always been there.

sentences.zh: 曩時北至臚朐河，南至邊境，人多散居，無所統壹，惟往來抄掠。

translations.literal: Formerly they ranged north to the Luchu River and south to the borderlands; people lived scattered without unified control and only raided back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier times they ranged north to the Luchu River and south to the frontier. Their people lived scattered, without unified rule, and raided one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 及太祖西征，至於流沙，阻卜望風悉降，西域諸國皆願入貢。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor campaigned west as far as the shifting sands, the Zubu submitted at the first wind, and the states of the Western Regions all wished to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu marched west as far as the shifting sands, the Zubu submitted at the first rumor of his approach, and the states of the Western Regions all offered tribute.

sentences.zh: 因遷種落，內置三部，以益吾國，不營城邑，不置戍兵，阻卜累世不敢為寇。

translations.literal: Tribes were then moved inward and three divisions were established within to strengthen our state; no walled towns were built and no garrison troops posted, and for generations the Zubu did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes were resettled inward, three divisions were established within our borders to strengthen the state, and no walled towns or garrison troops were needed. For generations the Zubu did not dare raid.

sentences.zh: 統和間，王太妃出師西域，拓土既遠，降附亦眾。

translations.literal: During Tonghe, the Queen Dowager Wang led troops into the Western Regions; territory was extended far, and submissions were many.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era Queen Dowager Wang campaigned in the Western Regions, extending territory far abroad and winning many submissions.

sentences.zh: 自後一部或叛，鄰部討之，使同力相制，正得馭遠人之道。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when one division rebelled, neighboring divisions were sent to punish it, making them restrain one another by shared force—the very way to govern distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when one division rebelled, neighboring divisions were sent to punish it, letting them restrain one another by force—the proper way to govern distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 及城可敦，開境數千里，西北之民，徭役日增，生業日殫。

translations.literal: When Kedun city was built and the border opened for thousands of li, the people of the northwest saw corvée increase daily and livelihoods daily exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kedun was fortified and the frontier stretched for thousands of li, northwestern subjects faced rising corvée and shrinking livelihoods day by day.

sentences.zh: 警急既不能救，叛服亦復不恒。

translations.literal: When emergencies arose they could not be relieved; submission and rebellion were no longer constant.
translations.idiomatic: Emergencies could not be met in time, and loyalty and rebellion alike grew unstable.

sentences.zh: 空有廣地之名，而無得地之實。

translations.literal: There was only the name of broad lands, without the reality of holding them.
translations.idiomatic: The realm held only the name of vast territory, not the reality of controlling it.

sentences.zh: 若貪土不已，漸至虛耗，其患有不勝言者。

translations.literal: If greed for land continues without end, gradual exhaustion will follow, and the harm is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: If the appetite for land never ends, the state will be drained little by little, and the harm is beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 況邊情不可深信，亦不可頓絕。

translations.literal: Moreover, frontier sentiment cannot be deeply trusted, yet it cannot be abruptly severed either.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier loyalties cannot be trusted completely, yet they cannot be cut off all at once.

sentences.zh: 得不為益，舍不為損。

translations.literal: What is gained may not be benefit; what is abandoned may not be loss.
translations.idiomatic: What is kept may not be gain; what is given up may not be loss.

sentences.zh: 國家大敵，惟在南方。

translations.literal: The state's great enemy lies only in the south.
translations.idiomatic: The state's gravest foe lies in the south alone.

sentences.zh: 今雖連和，難保他日。

translations.literal: Though we are allied now, it is hard to guarantee tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: We are at peace now, but tomorrow cannot be guaranteed.

sentences.zh: 若南方有變，屯戍遼邈，卒難赴援。

translations.literal: If trouble arises in the south, garrisons are remote and distant, and relief troops can hardly arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: If the south erupts in crisis, distant garrisons cannot send relief in time.

sentences.zh: 我進則敵退，我還則敵來，不可不慮也。

translations.literal: When we advance the enemy retreats; when we withdraw the enemy comes—this cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: When we advance, the enemy retreats; when we withdraw, the enemy returns. This cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 方今太平已久，正可恩結諸部，釋罪而歸地，內徙戍兵以增堡障，外明約束以正疆界。

translations.literal: Now that peace has lasted long, it is right to bind the tribes with grace, pardon offenses and return land, move garrison troops inward to strengthen fortifications, and outwardly clarify treaties to fix the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Peace has lasted long. Now is the time to win the tribes by grace, pardon offenses and return land, shift garrison troops inward to strengthen defenses, and set clear treaties to fix the borders.

sentences.zh: 每部各置酋長，歲修職貢。

translations.literal: Each division should have its own chief installed, with annual tribute duties observed.
translations.idiomatic: Each division should have its own chief, with annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 叛則討之，服則撫之。

translations.literal: If they rebel, punish them; if they submit, comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Punish rebellion; comfort submission.

sentences.zh: 諸部既安，必不生釁。

translations.literal: Once the tribes are settled, they will surely not create trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Once the tribes are settled, they will not stir trouble.

sentences.zh: 如是，則臣雖不能保其久而無變，知其必不深入侵掠也。

translations.literal: Thus, though your servant cannot guarantee that they will never change in the long run, I know they will certainly not launch deep invasions and raids.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot promise they will never change in the long run, but they will not launch deep raids.

sentences.zh: 或云棄地則損威，殊不知殫費竭財，以貪無用之地，使彼小部抗衡大國，萬一有敗，損威豈淺？

translations.literal: Some say abandoning land damages prestige, not knowing that exhausting wealth and draining treasuries to covet useless territory, letting small tribes contend with a great state—if defeat should come, would the loss of prestige be slight?
translations.idiomatic: Some say abandoning land damages prestige. They do not see that draining the treasury to seize useless ground and letting small tribes defy a great power—should defeat come once, would the loss of prestige be slight?

sentences.zh: 或又云，沃壤不可遽棄。

translations.literal: Others again say fertile soil cannot be hastily abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Others say fertile soil cannot be abandoned in haste.

sentences.zh: 臣以為土雖沃，民不能久居，一旦敵來，則不免內徙，豈可指為吾土而惜之？

translations.literal: Your servant holds that though the soil is fertile, the people cannot dwell there long; once enemies come, they must move inward—how can it be called our land and cherished?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that however fertile the soil, people cannot live there long. When enemies come, inhabitants must move inward. How can such land be called ours and cherished?

sentences.zh: 夫帑廩雖隨部而有，此特周急部民，一偏之惠，不能均濟天下。

translations.literal: Though treasury granaries exist division by division, this is only emergency relief for division subjects—a partial favor that cannot balance and aid the whole realm.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury granaries exist division by division, but they only relieve emergencies within each division—a partial favor that cannot aid the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 如欲均濟天下，則當知民困之由，而窒其隙。

translations.literal: If one wishes to balance and aid the whole realm, one must know the causes of the people's distress and block the openings through which it enters.
translations.idiomatic: To aid the whole realm, one must know why the people suffer and close the gaps through which distress enters.

sentences.zh: 節盤遊，簡驛傳，薄賦斂，戒奢侈。

translations.literal: Moderate hunting excursions, simplify courier posts, lighten taxes and levies, and guard against extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Moderate royal hunts, simplify courier service, lighten taxes, and restrain luxury.

sentences.zh: 期以數年，則困者可蘇，貧者可富矣。

translations.literal: Within a few years the distressed may revive and the poor may grow rich.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the distressed may recover and the poor may grow prosperous.

sentences.zh: 蓋民者國之本，兵者國之衛。

translations.literal: For the people are the root of the state, and soldiers are its guard.
translations.idiomatic: The people are the root of the state; soldiers are its shield.

sentences.zh: 兵不調則曠軍役，調之則損國本。

translations.literal: If troops are not levied, military service goes unfilled; if they are levied, the state's root is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: If troops are not levied, armies go unfilled; if they are levied, the state's root is harmed.

sentences.zh: 且諸部皆有補役之法。

translations.literal: Moreover, every division has a method of corvée replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Every division moreover has its corvée-replacement law.

sentences.zh: 昔補役始行，居者行者，類皆富實，故累世從戍，易為更代。

translations.literal: When corvée replacement first began, those who stayed home and those who went to service were mostly wealthy and solid, so families served for generations and rotation was easy.
translations.idiomatic: When corvée replacement began, households at home and on campaign were mostly well-off, so families could serve for generations and rotation was easy.

sentences.zh: 近歲邊虞數起，民多匱乏，既不任役事，隨補隨缺。

translations.literal: In recent years border alarms have arisen repeatedly; the people are largely impoverished, unable to bear service duties, and replacements are made only to fall vacant again at once.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years border alarms have multiplied. The people are impoverished, unable to bear service, and replacements fall vacant as soon as they are made.

sentences.zh: 茍無上戶，則中戶當之。

translations.literal: If there is no upper household, the middle household must take the duty.
translations.idiomatic: If no wealthy household remains, the middle household must answer the call.

sentences.zh: 曠日彌年，其窮益甚，所以取代為艱也。

translations.literal: Days stretch into years and their destitution grows worse—this is why rotation has become difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Days stretch into years and poverty deepens. That is why rotation has become so hard.

sentences.zh: 非惟補役如此，在邊戍兵亦然。

translations.literal: It is not only corvée replacement that is so; frontier garrison troops are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée replacement is not alone in this; frontier garrisons are the same.

sentences.zh: 譬如一抔之土，豈能填尋丈之壑！

translations.literal: It is like a handful of earth—how can it fill a ravine many feet deep and wide!
translations.idiomatic: It is like trying to fill a ravine many feet deep with a single handful of earth.

sentences.zh: 欲為長久之便，莫若使遠戍疲兵還於故鄉，薄其徭役，使人人給足，則補役之道可以復故也。

translations.literal: To secure long-term convenience, nothing is better than sending weary soldiers from distant garrisons back to their home districts, lightening their corvée, and making every man provisioned—then the way of corvée replacement can be restored.
translations.idiomatic: For lasting relief, send weary soldiers from distant garrisons home, lighten their corvée, and let every household become self-sufficient. Then corvée replacement can be restored.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞，自昔有國家者，不能無盜。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that from antiquity states have never been without bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has also heard that no state, from antiquity onward, has ever been without bandits.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，群黎雕弊，利於剽竊，良民往往化為凶暴。

translations.literal: In recent years the masses have been worn down; plunder and theft profit them, and good people often turn violent and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the people have been worn down. Plunder pays, and good citizens often turn violent.

sentences.zh: 甚者殺人無忌，至有亡命山澤，基亂首禍。

translations.literal: Some kill without restraint; some flee to mountains and marshes and become the seed of rebellion and the source of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Some kill without restraint; some flee to mountains and marshes and become the seeds of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 所謂民以困窮，皆為盜賊者，誠如聖慮。

translations.literal: The saying that when the people are distressed and poor they all become bandits is truly as Your Sagely Majesty has considered.
translations.idiomatic: The saying that poverty turns the people into bandits is exactly as Your Majesty has judged.

sentences.zh: 今欲芟夷本根，願陛下輕徭省役，使民務農。

translations.literal: Now, to cut the roots and branches, I wish Your Majesty would lighten corvée and reduce service, and make the people devote themselves to farming.
translations.idiomatic: To cut the evil at its root, Your Majesty should lighten corvée and labor and let the people devote themselves to farming.

sentences.zh: 衣食既足，安習教化，而重犯法，則民趨禮義，刑罰罕用矣。

translations.literal: When food and clothing are sufficient, they will peacefully accept instruction and transformation; and if lawbreaking is heavily punished, the people will turn to ritual and righteousness and punishments will rarely be used.
translations.idiomatic: When food and clothing are sufficient, they will accept instruction in peace. If lawbreaking is punished firmly, the people will turn to ritual and righteousness, and punishments will rarely be needed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞唐太宗問群臣治盜之方，皆曰：「嚴刑峻法。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang asked his ministers the method for governing bandits, and all said, "Severe punishments and stern laws."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang asked his ministers how to stop banditry. All answered, "Severe punishments and stern laws."

sentences.zh: 太宗笑曰：「寇盜所以滋者，由賦斂無度，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Taizong smiled and said, "Bandits multiply because levies are without limit and the people cannot sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong smiled and said, "Bandits multiply because taxes know no limit and the people cannot live.

sentences.zh: 今朕內省嗜欲，外罷遊幸，使海內安靜，則寇盜自止。」

translations.literal: Now I examine my desires within and cease excursions without, so that the realm within the seas is tranquil—then bandits will stop of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: If I restrain my desires within and cease excursions without, and let the realm be tranquil, bandits will stop of themselves."

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，寇盜多寡，皆由衣食豐儉，徭役重輕耳。

translations.literal: From this we see that whether bandits are many or few all depends on whether food and clothing are plentiful or scant and corvée heavy or light.
translations.idiomatic: From this we see that banditry rises or falls with the plenty or want of food and clothing and the weight or lightness of corvée.

sentences.zh: 今宜徙可敦城於近地，與西南副都部署烏古敵烈、隗烏古等部聲援相接。

translations.literal: Now Kedun city should be moved to a nearer site, linking its support with the Southwest Deputy Capital Military Commissioner and the Wugu, Dilie, Kui Wugu, and other divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Kedun should now be moved nearer, linking its support with the Southwest Deputy Capital Military Commissioner and the Wugu, Dilie, Kui Wugu, and allied divisions.

sentences.zh: 罷黑嶺二軍，並開、保州，皆隸東京。

translations.literal: The two armies of Heiling should be abolished, and Kai and Bao prefectures together placed under the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Disband the two Heiling armies and place Kai and Bao prefectures under the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 益東北戍軍及南京總管兵。

translations.literal: Increase the northeastern garrison troops and the Southern Capital commander's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Increase the northeastern garrison and the Southern Capital commander's forces.

sentences.zh: 增修壁壘，候尉相望，繕完樓櫓，浚治城隍，以為邊防。

translations.literal: Expand and repair ramparts, set watch posts in sight of one another, complete towers and parapets, and dredge moats and walls to serve as frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Expand the ramparts, set watch posts within sight of one another, repair towers and parapets, and dredge the moats to form a frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 此方今之急務也，願陛下裁之。

translations.literal: These are the urgent tasks of the present moment; I wish Your Majesty would decide upon them.
translations.idiomatic: These are the urgent tasks of the day. I beg Your Majesty to decide.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林都林牙，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy and concurrently charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Academician of the Hanlin Academy and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 仍詔諭之曰：「文章之職，國之光華，非才不用。

translations.literal: An edict also instructed him, saying, "The office of letters is the splendor of the state; without talent one is not employed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also told him, "The office of letters is the splendor of the state, and talent alone qualifies a man for it.

sentences.zh: 以卿文學，為時大儒，是用授卿以翰林之職。

translations.literal: Because of your literary learning, you are a great Confucian of the age; for this reason you are given the Hanlin post.
translations.idiomatic: Because of your literary learning you are among the great scholars of the age, and for that reason you are given the Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 朕之起居，悉以實錄。」

translations.literal: All my comings and goings are to be recorded in the Veritable Records."
translations.idiomatic: All my daily conduct is to be entered in the Veritable Records."

sentences.zh: 自是日見親信，每入侍，賜坐。

translations.literal: From then on he was daily seen in favor and trust; whenever he entered attendance he was granted a seat.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he grew daily in favor. Whenever he attended the emperor he was granted a seat.

sentences.zh: 遇勝日，帝與飲酒賦詩，以相酬酢，君臣相得無比。

translations.literal: On fine days the emperor drank and composed poetry with him, exchanging verses; ruler and minister were matched as never before.
translations.idiomatic: On pleasant days the emperor drank and wrote poetry with him, exchanging verses in perfect harmony between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 韓家奴知無不言，雖諧謔不忘規諷。

translations.literal: Hanjianu spoke without reserve on what he knew; even in jest and banter he did not forget remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjianu spoke his mind on every matter he knew, and even in jest he never forgot to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 韓家奴每見帝獵，未嘗不諫。

translations.literal: Whenever Hanjianu saw the emperor hunt, he never failed to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hanjianu saw the emperor go hunting, he remonstrated without fail.

sentences.zh: 會有司奏獵秋山，熊虎傷死數十人，韓家奴書於冊。

translations.literal: Once the relevant offices reported a hunt on Autumn Mountain in which bears and tigers killed and wounded several dozen men; Hanjianu wrote it in the register.
translations.idiomatic: Once the relevant offices reported a hunt on Autumn Mountain in which bears and tigers killed or wounded several dozen men. Hanjianu entered it in the register.

sentences.zh: 帝見，命去之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw it and ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the entry and ordered it struck out.

sentences.zh: 韓家奴既出，復書。

translations.literal: After Hanjianu left, he wrote it in again.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanjianu left the hall, he wrote it in again.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝見之曰：「史筆當如是。」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor saw it and said, "The historian's brush ought to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor saw it and said, "A historian's brush ought to work like this."

sentences.zh: 帝問韓家奴：「我國家創業以來，孰為賢主？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Hanjianu, "Since our state was founded, which ruler has been worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Hanjianu, "Since our state was founded, which ruler has been the worthiest?"

sentences.zh: 韓家奴以穆宗對。

translations.literal: Hanjianu answered with Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjianu named Muzong.

sentences.zh: 帝怪之曰：「穆宗嗜酒，喜怒不常，視人猶草芥，卿何謂賢？」

translations.literal: The emperor wondered and said, "Muzong was addicted to wine, his joy and anger were inconstant, and he regarded men like grass—why do you call him worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and said, "Muzong was addicted to wine, his moods were erratic, and he treated men like weeds. Why do you call him worthy?"

sentences.zh: 韓家奴對曰：「穆宗雖暴虐，省徭輕賦，人樂其生。

translations.literal: Hanjianu replied, "Though Muzong was cruel and violent, he reduced corvée and lightened levies, and the people rejoiced in their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Hanjianu answered, "Muzong was cruel, yet he reduced corvée and lightened taxes, and the people were glad to live.

sentences.zh: 終穆之世，無罪被戮，未有過今日秋山傷死者。

translations.literal: Throughout Muzong's reign no innocent person was executed, and nothing exceeded today's dead and wounded on Autumn Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Muzong's reign no innocent person was executed, and nothing matched today's dead and wounded on Autumn Mountain.

sentences.zh: 臣故以穆宗為賢。」

translations.literal: For this reason your servant holds Muzong worthy."
translations.idiomatic: For that reason your servant holds Muzong worthy."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 詔與耶律庶成錄遙輦可汗至重熙以來事跡，集為二十卷，進之。

translations.literal: He was ordered with Yelu Shucheng to record events from the Yaolian khans down through Chongxi, compile them into twenty scrolls, and present them.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Yelu Shucheng to compile events from the Yaolian khans through the Chongxi era into twenty scrolls and present them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復詔曰：「古之治天下者，明禮義，正法度。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year another edict said, "Those who governed the realm in antiquity clarified ritual and righteousness and rectified law and measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year another edict said, "Ancient rulers of the realm clarified ritual and righteousness and set law and measure in order.

sentences.zh: 我朝之興，世有明德，雖中外向化，然禮書未作，無以示後世。

translations.literal: Since our dynasty rose, each generation has had bright virtue; though within and without all have turned to our transformation, yet no book of ritual has been composed, and there is nothing to show later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Since our dynasty rose, each generation has shown bright virtue. Though within and without all have submitted, no book of ritual has been written, and we have nothing to show posterity.

sentences.zh: 卿可與庶成酌古準今，制為禮典。

translations.literal: You may with Shucheng weigh antiquity against the present and formulate a ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: You and Shucheng should weigh antiquity against the present and draft a ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 事或有疑，與北、南院同議。」

translations.literal: If matters are doubtful, deliberate together with the Northern and Southern Courts."
translations.idiomatic: Where matters are doubtful, consult the Northern and Southern Courts."

sentences.zh: 韓家奴既被詔，博考經籍，自天子達於庶人，情文制度可行於世，不繆於古者，撰成三卷，進之。

translations.literal: Once Hanjianu received the edict, he broadly examined the classics and histories; from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, whatever in sentiment, text, and institutions could be practiced in the world without straying from antiquity he compiled into three scrolls and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hanjianu received the edict, he examined the classics broadly. Whatever in sentiment, text, and institutions from the Son of Heaven down to the common people could be practiced in the world without straying from antiquity he compiled into three scrolls and presented them.

sentences.zh: 又詔譯諸書，韓家奴欲帝知古今成敗，譯《通曆》、《貞觀政要》、《五代史》。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to translate various books; Hanjianu wished the emperor to know success and failure through past and present, and translated the Tongli, the Zhenguan Zhengyao, and the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to translate books. Wishing the emperor to know success and failure through past and present, Hanjianu translated the Tongli, the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign, and the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 時帝以其老，不任朝謁，拜歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, considering him old and unable to bear court attendance, appointed him Military Commissioner of Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering him too old for regular court attendance, appointed him Military Commissioner of Guide Army.

sentences.zh: 以善治聞。

translations.literal: He became known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for governing well.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使問勞，韓家奴表謝。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to inquire after him; Hanjianu submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to inquire after him, and Hanjianu submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 召修國史，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He was summoned to resume compiling the national history, then died at seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned back to compile the national history and died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 有《六義集》十二卷行於世。

translations.literal: His Collected Writings on the Six Principles in twelve scrolls circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Writings on the Six Principles in twelve scrolls circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 李澣，初仕晉為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Li Han first served the Jin as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han first served the Later Jin as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 晉亡歸遼，當太宗崩、世宗立，恟渙不定，澣與高勛等十餘人羈留南京。

translations.literal: When Jin fell he returned to Liao; as the Taizong Emperor died and the Shizong Emperor was enthroned, turmoil was unsettled, and Han together with Gao Xun and more than ten others were detained at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin fell he entered Liao service. As Emperor Taizong died and Emperor Shizong was enthroned, the realm was unsettled, and Han with Gao Xun and more than ten others were detained at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 久之，從歸上京，授翰林學士。

translations.literal: After a long while he followed the court back to the Supreme Capital and was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he followed the court back to the Supreme Capital and was made Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，累遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, he rose step by step to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時澣兄濤在汴為翰林學士，密遣人召澣。

translations.literal: At that time Han's elder brother Tao was Hanlin Academician at Bian and secretly sent someone to summon Han.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han's elder brother Tao was Hanlin Academician at Bianjing and secretly sent someone to summon him.

sentences.zh: 澣得書，托求醫南京，易服夜出，欲遁歸汴。

translations.literal: Han received the letter, pleaded illness to seek medical treatment at the Southern Capital, changed clothes and went out at night, intending to flee back to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Han received the letter, pleaded illness to seek treatment at the Southern Capital, changed clothes, slipped out at night, and tried to flee back to Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 至涿，為僥巡者所得，送之南京，下吏。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhuo he was seized by patrol scouts, sent to the Southern Capital, and handed over to the magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuo he was seized by patrol scouts, sent to the Southern Capital, and handed over to the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 澣伺獄吏熟寢，以衣帶自經；

translations.literal: Han waited until the prison officers were fast asleep, then hanged himself with his belt;
translations.idiomatic: Han waited until the jailers were fast asleep, then hanged himself with his belt;

sentences.zh: 不死，防之愈嚴。

translations.literal: he did not die, and his guard was made stricter still.
translations.idiomatic: he did not die, and his guard was tightened further.

sentences.zh: 械赴上京，自投潢河中流，為鐵索牽掣，又不死。

translations.literal: Fettered, he was sent to the Supreme Capital; he threw himself into midstream of the Huang River and was pulled back by iron chains, yet again did not die.
translations.idiomatic: In fetters he was sent to the Supreme Capital. He threw himself into midstream of the Huang River, was pulled back on iron chains, and still did not die.

sentences.zh: 及抵上京，帝欲殺之。

translations.literal: When he reached the Supreme Capital the emperor wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the Supreme Capital the emperor wished to kill him.

sentences.zh: 時高勛已為樞密使，救止之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Xun was already Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and rescued him, stopping the execution.
translations.idiomatic: By then Gao Xun was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and stopped the execution.

sentences.zh: 屢言於上曰：「澣本非負恩，以母年八十，急於省覲致罪。

translations.literal: He repeatedly told the throne, "Han did not originally betray favor; his mother is eighty years old, and in his urgency to visit her he incurred guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He told the throne repeatedly, "Han did not betray your favor. His mother is eighty, and in his urgency to visit her he committed this offense.

sentences.zh: 且澣富於文學，方今少有倫比，若留掌詞命，可以增光國體。」

translations.literal: Moreover Han is rich in literary learning; today few can be compared with him. If he is kept to manage edicts and commands, he can add luster to the state's dignity."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Han is rich in literary learning and has few equals today. If he is kept to manage edicts and commands, he can add luster to the state."

sentences.zh: 帝怒稍解，仍令禁錮於奉國寺，凡六年，艱苦萬狀。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, yet he still ordered Han confined at Fengguo Temple for six years in every kind of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased somewhat, but Han was still confined at Fengguo Temple for six years in every kind of hardship.

sentences.zh: 會上欲建《太宗功德碑》，高勛奏曰：「非李澣無可秉筆者。」

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to erect the Stele of Taizong's Merits and Virtues, Gao Xun memorialized, "Apart from Li Han there is no one fit to wield the brush."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to erect the Stele of Emperor Taizong's Merits and Virtues, Gao Xun memorialized, "Apart from Li Han there is no one fit to wield the brush."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 文成以進，上悅，釋囚。

translations.literal: When the text was completed and presented, the emperor was pleased and released the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the text was completed and presented, the emperor was pleased and released him.

sentences.zh: 尋加禮部尚書，宣政殿學士，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made Minister of Rites and Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Rites and Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall, then died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：統和、重熙之間，務修文治，而韓家奴對策，落落累數百言，概可施諸行事，亦遼之晁、賈哉。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Between Tonghe and Chongxi the court devoted itself to civil governance, and Hanjianu's policy response, flowing freely for several hundred words, could in general be applied in action—was he not Liao's Chao Cuo and Jia Yi?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Between the Tonghe and Chongxi eras the court devoted itself to civil governance. Hanjianu's policy response, flowing freely for several hundred words, could in general be put into practice. Was he not Liao's Chao Cuo and Jia Yi?

sentences.zh: 李澣雖以詞章見稱，而其進退不足論矣。

translations.literal: Though Li Han was famed for literary composition, his comings and goings are not worth discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li Han was famed for literary composition, his career of advance and retreat is hardly worth discussing.
